title: Film & Television
description: Fifty lines of dialogue from films and series, sourced from Wikiquote.

attribution.note: Quote text and attributions come from Wikiquote's sourced sections and are used under CC BY-SA 4.0. Redistribution must preserve this attribution and license.

quotes.text: Of all the gin joints in all the towns in all the world, she walks into mine.
quotes.note: Nine words that turn coincidence into fate.
quotes.writer: Julius J. Epstein, Philip G. Epstein and Howard Koch

quotes.text: Here's looking at you, kid.
quotes.note: A toast reused across the film until it becomes a farewell.
quotes.writer: Julius J. Epstein, Philip G. Epstein and Howard Koch

quotes.text: I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse.
quotes.note: Menace delivered entirely through understatement.
quotes.writer: Mario Puzo and Francis Ford Coppola
quotes.speaker: Vito

quotes.text: Leave the gun. Take the Cannoli.
quotes.note: Two imperatives, and the second one does all the characterisation.
quotes.writer: Mario Puzo and Francis Ford Coppola

quotes.text: If the headline is big enough, it makes the news big enough.
quotes.note: A newspaperman's ethics stated as a production rule.
quotes.writer: Herman J. Mankiewicz and Orson Welles

quotes.text: I don't think there's one word that can describe a man's life.
quotes.note: The film's own thesis, spoken by a minor character.
quotes.writer: Herman J. Mankiewicz and Orson Welles

quotes.text: I am big. It's the pictures that got small.
quotes.note: Self-delusion and accurate criticism in the same breath.
quotes.speaker: Norma Desmond

quotes.text: We didn't need dialogue. We had faces!
quotes.note: An argument for silent film, made in dialogue.

quotes.text: Well, nobody's perfect!
quotes.note: The most casual possible response to a revelation. Perfect last line.
quotes.writer: Billy Wilder and I. A. L. Diamond
quotes.speaker: Osgood

quotes.text: Fasten your seatbelts, it's going to be a bumpy night.
quotes.note: A warning issued by someone who intends to cause the turbulence.

quotes.text: So many people know me. I wish I did. I wish someone would tell me about me.
quotes.note: Fame described as a form of self-estrangement.

quotes.text: I want you to get up right now and go to the window, open it, and stick your head out, and yell: I'M AS MAD AS HELL, AND I'M NOT GOING TO TAKE THIS ANYMORE!
quotes.note: A line that escaped the film and became a political slogan.

quotes.text: Forget it, Jake. It's Chinatown.
quotes.note: Consolation and verdict at once. The place explains the crime.
quotes.speaker: Lawrence Walsh

quotes.text: You're dumber than you think I think you are.
quotes.note: An insult that requires a moment of arithmetic.

quotes.text: I love the smell of napalm in the morning.
quotes.note: Horror rendered as connoisseurship.
quotes.writer: John Milius and Francis Ford Coppola

quotes.text: I've seen things you people wouldn't believe. Attack ships on fire off shoulder of Orion. I watched c-beams glitter in the dark near the Tannhäuser Gate. All those moments will be lost in time, like tears in rain. Time to die.
quotes.note: Improvised on set, and the best-known lines in the film.

quotes.text: Quite an experience to live in fear, isn't it? That's what it is to be a slave.
quotes.note: The antagonist explaining his own condition to his hunter.

quotes.text: I'm sorry, Dave. I'm afraid I can't do that.
quotes.note: Politeness as the delivery mechanism for menace.
quotes.writer: Stanley Kubrick and Arthur C. Clarke
quotes.speaker: HAL

quotes.text: By the way, do you mind if I ask you a personal question?
quotes.note: A machine performing social nicety, which is the whole horror.
quotes.writer: Stanley Kubrick and Arthur C. Clarke
quotes.speaker: HAL

quotes.text: Hello, my name is Inigo Montoya. You killed my father. Prepare to die.
quotes.note: A formula repeated so often it becomes incantation.
quotes.speaker: Inigo

quotes.text: You keep using that word. I do not think it means what you think it means. My God, he's climbing.
quotes.note: A running joke about the precision of language.
quotes.speaker: Inigo

quotes.text: What would you do if you were stuck in one place, and every day was exactly the same, and nothing that you did mattered?
quotes.note: The premise stated as an idle question before it becomes literal.
quotes.speaker: Phil

quotes.text: There's more to life than a little money, you know.
quotes.note: The film's moral, delivered without emphasis.

quotes.text: Yeah, well, the Dude abides.
quotes.note: Two words that function as an entire philosophy.
quotes.speaker: The Dude

quotes.text: I finally get a bouquet and it's a goodbye present. That's depressing.
quotes.note: A child's flat reading of a sentimental gesture.

quotes.text: If you completely forget your name, you'll never find your way back home. I've tried everything to remember mine.
quotes.note: Memory framed as something that persists beneath recall.
quotes.speaker: Haku

quotes.text: I loved you on this day. I love this memory.
quotes.note: Present tense and past tense in the same thought.
quotes.work: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind

quotes.text: "Blessed are the forgetful: for they get the better even of their blunders."
quotes.note: A Nietzsche quotation used as the film's thesis.
quotes.work: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind

quotes.text: But then the morning comes, and we turn back into pumpkins, right?
quotes.note: A fairy-tale figure used to name a deadline.

quotes.text: For relaxing times, make it Suntory time.
quotes.note: A translation that has clearly lost most of its original.

quotes.text: The more you know who you are, and what you want, the less you let things upset you.
quotes.note: Advice given across a thirty-year age gap.
quotes.speaker: Bob

quotes.text: You ain't got to love me, but you gonna know that I love you.
quotes.note: Love stated as a fact the listener does not get to negotiate.

quotes.text: At some point, you gotta decide for yourself who you're going to be. Can't let nobody make that decision for you.
quotes.note: The film's central instruction, given early and paid off late.
quotes.speaker: Juan

quotes.text: What are you, a family of charlatans?
quotes.note: An accusation that is entirely accurate.

quotes.text: You know what kind of plan never fails? No plan.
quotes.note: Fatalism disguised as strategy.

quotes.text: If Snot Boogie always stole the money, why'd you let him play?
quotes.note: The question that opens the series and states its whole theme.
quotes.speaker: McNulty

quotes.text: Ayo, lesson here, Bey. You come at the king, you best not miss.
quotes.note: Street proverb compressed to six words.
quotes.speaker: Omar

quotes.text: Don't make me an optimist, you will ruin my life.
quotes.note: A refusal of comfort, played as a joke and meant seriously.
quotes.speaker: Fleabag

quotes.text: I'm Janet. I'm the informational assistant here in the Good Place.
quotes.note: Exposition delivered by a character who is herself the exposition.
quotes.speaker: Janet

quotes.text: I mean, somebody royally forked up. Somebody forked up. Why can't I say "fork"?
quotes.note: A world-building rule turned into a running gag.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor

quotes.text: It is good to be here, Charlie. Sorry I was late. The traffic...
quotes.note: A talk-show entrance that establishes the whole character.
quotes.speaker: BoJack
quotes.episode: BoJack Horseman: The BoJack Horseman Story, Chapter One

quotes.text: There's always money in the banana stand.
quotes.note: A line whose payoff arrives an entire season later.
quotes.speaker: George Sr.

quotes.text: You want your belt to buckle, not your chair.
quotes.note: Advice that reveals everything about who is giving it.
quotes.speaker: Lucille Bluth

quotes.text: It's sourdough starter. I thought that you might like to make something.
quotes.note: An absurd gift standing in for a family's inability to speak.
quotes.speaker: Connor Roy

quotes.text: Gentlemen, you can't fight in here! This is the War Room!
quotes.note: Absurdity stated with total institutional seriousness.

quotes.text: I'll have what she's having.
quotes.note: The best-known punchline in romantic comedy, from a bystander.
quotes.speaker: Older Woman Customer

quotes.text: Let me tell you the story of right hand-left hand.
quotes.note: A parable told with the hands.

quotes.text: The past is just a story we tell ourselves.
quotes.note: Memory reframed as authorship.

quotes.text: Don't you think maybe they are the same thing? Love and attention?
quotes.note: A question that reframes the entire film in six words.
quotes.speaker: Sister Sarah Joan

quotes.text: It’s very hard to keep personal prejudice out of a thing like this. And no matter where you run into it, prejudice obscures the truth.
quotes.note: The film's thesis, delivered plainly near the end.
